english-q4_k.expected_text: At sunrise, the coastal library opened its doors for a week of community work. Volunteers carried boxes through the reading room, where tall windows warmed the tables. One team repaired damaged books and photographed their covers, while a retired teacher sorted harbour letters and students copied names from a faded register. Near the entrance, a carpenter tightened chairs and built a stand for local newspapers; by midday, strangers shared memories of storms, concerts, and friends who had moved away. In the afternoon, they arranged a children’s reading corner and a quiet desk for language learners. Before closing, Mara listed the remaining work: mend the clock, finish the catalogue, repaint the sign, and ask the council about a safer ramp. The volunteers agreed to return on Saturday with better tools and more books, because patient work had made the building useful again.

Volunteers moved boxes through the hall, cleaned display cases, and labelled objects from the basement. Everyone agreed to return with better tools and more photographs, because patient work had given the museum a future.
